claims.text: In CoCrFeMnNi-based high-entropy alloys, toughness retention is governed by the controlled formation and uniform dispersion of nano-oxides.
An optimal oxygen partial pressure during melting produces a fine, uniform nano-oxide dispersion in CoCrFeMnNi-based alloys.
Dispersed nano-oxides deflect developing cracks and impede crack propagation.
Excessive oxygen causes oxide particles to agglomerate into larger clusters.
Large oxide clusters act as stress concentrators and crack-initiation sites.
Oxide clustering reduces toughness and causes premature failure.
CoCrFeMnNi-based material melted in an oxygen-free inert atmosphere has minimal oxide formation.
Oxygen partial pressure will be varied from 10^-4 atm to 10^-2 atm during melting.
Nano-oxide size, distribution, and volume fraction are the structural variables mediating toughness.
Samples processed at an optimal oxygen partial pressure will have greater fracture toughness or fracture energy than oxygen-free or uncontrolled-oxygen baselines.
Samples processed at an optimal oxygen partial pressure will exhibit delayed crack propagation relative to the baseline.
The proposed behavior should hold for CoCrFeMnNi-based alloys over oxygen partial pressures from 10^-4 atm to 10^-2 atm.
Toughness enhancement requires nano-oxides to remain below a critical size and uniformly dispersed.
The optimal oxygen level, critical nano-oxide size, and required distribution parameters are not yet established.
Nano-oxide characteristics and toughness can be compared across controlled oxygen levels using microscopy, fracture-toughness testing, impact testing, and fractography.
Failure to observe improved toughness at the putative optimal oxygen level, or failure to observe clustering and reduced toughness at excessive oxygen, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The conditions require avoiding processing that produces large clustered oxides, whereas the predicted excessive-oxygen branch and falsification experiment require producing and observing oxide clustering. Applied to every sample, the stated condition would prevent testing that branch.
